quizzes.title: Identity Papers and Citizenship
quizzes.passage: Citizenship is the legal recognition of an individual as a member of a state. It grants rights and privileges, and it requires allegiance. In India, citizenship defines who holds these rights and follows citizenship laws. Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship provisions. Those provisions specify who became citizens when the Constitution came into force. The Citizenship Act, 1955 outlines the ways in which citizenship can be acquired, and the conditions under which it can be lost. Many Indians carry papers that record personal details. These papers are issued by different authorities for different purposes, such as access to services or travel. Each one is issued under its own rules and for its own function. On Passport Seva Divas, the Ministry of External Affairs clarified that an Indian passport is primarily a travel document. In Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978), the passport was recognised as a travel document subject to constitutional protections. The Passports Act, 1967 provides for the issue of passports by the Central Government. Several provisions of the Constitution concern rights. Article 19 protects freedom of speech and expression, Article 15 prohibits discrimination on various grounds, and Article 30 grants rights to establish educational institutions.

questions.q: What does Aadhaar serve as proof of?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Aadhaar is proof of identity and residence, not citizenship.

questions.q: Which document is said to establish electoral eligibility but not citizenship?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Voter ID establishes electoral eligibility and does not establish citizenship.

questions.q: Which persons are issued a Citizenship Certificate?
options: Only those who acquired citizenship through registration or naturalisation
Only those who acquired citizenship by birth
Only those who acquired citizenship by descent
All persons holding a valid Indian passport
questions.explanation: A Citizenship Certificate is issued only to persons acquiring citizenship through registration or naturalisation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Deletion of a name from the electoral roll does not amount to loss of citizenship.
Reason (R): The Election Commission of India determines electoral eligibility, not citizenship.
In the context of the above, which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Electoral eligibility is decided by the Election Commission, so removal from the roll is an electoral matter and not a loss of citizenship.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Ration Card   ->   C. Presumption of citizenship from electoral roll inclusion
II. Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995)   ->   A. Referral to Ministry of Home Affairs
III. Citizenship Rules, 2003   ->   B. Residence and welfare eligibility
IV. Suspected citizenship cases   ->   D. National Register of Indian Citizens
questions.explanation: The Ration Card, the 1995 case, the 2003 Citizenship Rules and suspected-case referral match B, C, D and A respectively.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. No single universal document conclusively proves Indian citizenship.
II. India permits dual citizenship for persons who hold citizenship of another country.
III. A Ration Card establishes electoral eligibility.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since India does not permit dual citizenship and a Ration Card indicates residence and welfare eligibility.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Sarbananda Sonowal vs Union of India (2005) placed the burden of proving Indian citizenship on the person claiming it.
II. Inclusion in the electoral roll creates a presumption of citizenship that cannot be displaced by any process.
III. Persons acquiring citizenship by birth or descent receive a Citizenship Certificate.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the presumption can be displaced through due legal process and birth or descent does not bring a certificate.

quizzes.title: Proving Citizenship Status
quizzes.passage: Indian citizenship is a legal status. It makes a person a member of the state and carries rights, privileges and obligations. The Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955 govern the matter, and together they set out how the status is acquired and how it may be lost. Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship at the time the Constitution came into force. Other provisions concern rights, including Article 19 on freedom of speech and expression and Article 30 on the right to establish educational institutions. Records issued to Indians serve everyday purposes. They are used to show a person's details when dealing with government agencies, and some are used in public processes. Each record is issued under its own rules for a particular function, so its scope is limited to that function. Passports are one such record. The Ministry of External Affairs clarified on Passport Seva Divas that an Indian passport is primarily a travel document, and Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978) recognised it as a travel document subject to constitutional protections. Questions of citizenship have also come before the courts. Judgments have examined how the status is proved and what follows when a person's name is removed from a list kept for another purpose. Where a doubt about status arises, it is decided through the procedure set by law.

questions.q: Which 2005 case placed the burden of proving Indian citizenship on the person claiming it? (give the first party's name)
accept: Sarbananda Sonowal vs Union of India
questions.explanation: Sarbananda Sonowal vs Union of India (2005) placed the burden of proof on the claimant.

questions.q: Which 1995 case held that inclusion in the electoral roll creates a presumption of citizenship? (give the first party's name)
accept: Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer
questions.explanation: Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995) created that presumption.

questions.q: Aadhaar is proof of identity and of which other attribute, but not of citizenship? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Aadhaar as proof of identity and residence, not citizenship.

questions.q: A Ration Card indicates residence and eligibility for which purpose? (two words)
questions.explanation: A Ration Card indicates residence and eligibility for welfare benefits, not citizenship.

questions.q: To which ministry must suspected citizenship cases be referred for adjudication under the Citizenship Act, 1955? (acronym or full name)
questions.explanation: Suspected citizenship cases must be referred to the Ministry of Home Affairs under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

questions.q: What is the name of the register of Indian citizens envisaged under the Citizenship Rules, 2003? (full name)
questions.explanation: The Citizenship Rules 2003 envisaged a National Register of Indian Citizens.

questions.q: Citizenship Certificates are issued only to persons who acquired citizenship through which two processes? (give the two processes, joined by 'and')
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Citizenship Certificate is issued only to persons acquiring citizenship through registration or naturalisation.

quizzes.title: Assam Settlement and Register
quizzes.passage: Citizenship is the legal recognition of an individual as a member of a state. It grants rights and privileges, and it requires allegiance. In India, citizenship defines who holds these rights and follows citizenship laws. Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship provisions. The Citizenship Act, 1955 outlines the ways in which citizenship can be acquired, and the conditions under which it can be lost. Assam has its own history on the question. A long agitation in the state was carried on by several organisations over a number of years, and it was eventually resolved through a written settlement. The settlement was followed by a committee formed by the Central Government to work out how its commitments could be put into practice. The committee made a set of recommendations for the governments concerned, and the state government approved a large share of them. Assam also has a register of citizens, which is prepared through a verification process that applicants go through. The Constitution also contains provisions on rights. Article 19 protects freedom of speech and expression, Article 15 prohibits discrimination on various grounds, Article 16 deals with public employment, and Article 30 grants rights to establish educational institutions.

questions.q: The Assam agitation that ended with a Memorandum of Settlement was directed against which of the following?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the agitation led by AASU and AAGSP was directed against illegal immigration.

questions.q: The committee headed by Justice (Retd) Biplab Kumar Sarma submitted how many recommendations?
questions.explanation: The committee submitted 67 recommendations.

questions.q: The NRC in Assam commenced in 2003 following which of the following?
options: An order of the Supreme Court
A decision of the Assam Cabinet
questions.explanation: The NRC in Assam commenced in 2003 following a Supreme Court order.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Applicants for the NRC in Assam had to establish links with legacy records.
Reason (R): The legacy records had to postdate the Assam Accord.
In the context of the above, which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The assertion is true, but the legacy records had to predate 24 March 1971, not postdate the Accord.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. AASU   ->   B. All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad
II. AAGSP   ->   A. 1951
III. Tripartite Memorandum of Settlement   ->   D. All Assam Students' Union
IV. First NRC in Assam   ->   C. 15 August 1985
questions.explanation: AASU is the All Assam Students' Union, AAGSP is the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad, the Memorandum was signed on 15 August 1985 and the first NRC was in 1951.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Memorandum of Settlement was signed by the Central Government and the Assam Government alone.
II. The Assam agitation lasted from 1979 to 1985.
III. The first NRC in Assam was conducted in 1971.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement II is correct, since the agitation leaders also signed the Memorandum and the first NRC in Assam was in 1951.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Applicants in the Assam NRC had to link themselves to legacy records predating 24 March 1971.
II. The NRC in Assam commenced in 1951 following a Supreme Court order.
III. The Assam agitation was led by the Assam Government against illegal immigration.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the NRC commenced in 2003 and the agitation was led by AASU and AAGSP, not by the state government.

quizzes.title: Assam Accord and NRC Facts
quizzes.passage: In India, citizenship is governed by Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution and by the Citizenship Act, 1955. Citizenship is the legal recognition of an individual as a member of a state, and it grants rights and privileges, and it also requires allegiance. The Act lists several ways of acquiring citizenship, including birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory, and it also sets out the conditions for losing it, such as renunciation, termination and deprivation. Assam has a history of agitation on questions of identity. A long movement in the state was carried on by several organisations over a number of years. It was eventually resolved through a written settlement, which set out commitments for the future. The settlement was followed by a committee, formed to work out how those commitments could be put into practice. The committee made recommendations, and the state government approved a large share of them. Assam also has a register of citizens. It is prepared through a verification process that applicants go through. Separately, the Constitution contains rights provisions: Article 19 protects freedom of speech and expression, Article 15 prohibits discrimination on various grounds, Article 16 deals with public employment, and Article 30 grants rights to establish educational institutions.

questions.q: Between which two years did the Assam agitation take place? (give as YYYY-YYYY)
questions.explanation: The Assam agitation ran from 1979 to 1985.

questions.q: What is the full form of AASU? (full name)
questions.explanation: AASU stands for All Assam Students' Union.

questions.q: What is the full form of AAGSP? (full name)
questions.explanation: AAGSP stands for All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad.

questions.q: On what date (day, month and year) was the Tripartite Memorandum of Settlement signed? (date)
questions.explanation: The Tripartite Memorandum of Settlement was signed on August 15, 1985.

questions.q: Which Justice (Retd) headed the committee set up to operationalise the Assam settlement? (name)
questions.explanation: The committee was headed by Justice (Retd) Biplab Kumar Sarma.

questions.q: In which year did the NRC in Assam commence following a Supreme Court order? (year)
questions.explanation: The NRC in Assam commenced in 2003 following a Supreme Court order.

questions.q: In which year was the first NRC in Assam conducted? (year)
questions.explanation: The first NRC in Assam was conducted in 1951.
